reconstruction: Composite natural setting on the existing game terrain, not a surveyed historic site. Present-day geology and native habitat references establish materials and forms, not an exact nineteenth-century view. Holdings remain separately sourced game pieces.
brief: Full natural-strength ochre and rusty red clay, tan sandstone gravel and exposed rock. Fine granular surface and irregular erosion bands; no snow, broad green lawn, modern infrastructure, invented tribal imagery or transplanted saguaro. Preserve existing terrain and collision. First pass uses the existing exposed rocks and ground surface; additional plants or large formations are outside this pass.

sources.claim: Red Painted Desert badlands have sparse vegetation; shadscale and fluffgrass occur there. Adjacent grassland and shrubland are distinct habitats.
Colourful bentonite badlands erode into rolling hills; resistant sandstone caps softer clay.

uncertainties: Exact RGB values and soil distribution are artistic reconstruction.
Existing rock shapes are retained as a stylized composite, not identified local specimens.
